### 4.1 Adenohypophyseal Hormones & Target Actions

| Pituitary Hormone | Secretory Cell Type | Target Gland / Tissue | Primary Physiological Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Growth Hormone (GH / Somatotropin)** | Somatotrophs | Liver, Bones, Skeletal Muscle | Stimulates liver production of **IGF-1 (Somatomedin C)**; promotes somatic tissue growth, protein synthesis, and lipolysis |
| **Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)** | Thyrotrophs | Thyroid Follicular Cells | Stimulates synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones ($T_3$ and $T_4$) |
| **Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH)** | Corticotrophs | Adrenal Cortex (*Zona Fasciculata*) | Stimulates synthesis and release of **Glucocorticoids (Cortisol)** |
| **Prolactin (PRL)** | Lactotrophs | Mammary Glands | Stimulates mammary gland growth and milk synthesis *(inhibited by dopamine)* |
| **Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)** | Gonadotrophs | Ovarian Follicles / Sertoli Cells | Females: Growth of ovarian follicles; Males: Stimulates spermatogenesis |
| **Luteinizing Hormone (LH / ICSH)** | Gonadotrophs | Corpus Luteum / Leydig Cells | Females: Triggers **Ovulation** and forms Corpus Luteum; Males: Stimulates Leydig cells to produce **Testosterone** |
| **Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH)** | Pars Intermedia | Dermal Melanocytes | Acts on skin melanocytes to regulate melanin synthesis and pigmentation |

### 4.2 Neurohypophyseal Hormones (Synthesized in Hypothalamus)
- **Oxytocin**: Synthesized in hypothalamic Paraventricular Nuclei.
  1. **Parturition**: Stimulates vigorous contractions of uterine smooth muscle during labor (**Ferguson Reflex**).
  2. **Lactation**: Stimulates myoepithelial cell contraction in mammary alveoli for **Milk Ejection / Let-down Reflex**.
- **Vasopressin / Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH)**: Synthesized in hypothalamic Supraoptic Nuclei. Inserts **Aquaporin-2** channels into kidney DCT and collecting ducts to promote water reabsorption and prevent diuresis.

conceptBreakdown.heading: IGF-1 / Somatomedin C Mediation
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Growth hormone (GH) exerts most of its systemic skeletal and chondrocyte growth-promoting actions indirectly via hepatic synthesis and secretion of Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1 / Somatomedin C).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Diabetes Insipidus vs Diabetes Mellitus
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Diabetes Insipidus is caused by neurogenic ADH deficiency or nephrogenic ADH receptor insensitivity, causing massive polyuria of dilute, sugar-free urine. Diabetes Mellitus involves insulin deficiency/resistance with hyperglycemia, glucosuria, and ketonuria.
